identity.name: ONESOURCE SPECL PHARMA L
identity.industry: Pharma / Specialty CDMO & GLP-1 Drug Device Contract Manufacturing

summary.oneLiner: Revenue declined 26% YoY due to Canadian semaglutide approval delays delaying commercial supply, but underlying demand and order book remain robust; FY28 $400M revenue and $160M EBITDA guidance reaffirmed as capacity expansion and biosimilar funnel accelerate, positioning for material CSA revenue ramp from H2 FY27.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined 26% YoY due to Canadian semaglutide approval delays delaying commercial supply, but underlying demand and order book remain robust; FY28 $400M revenue and $160M EBITDA guidance reaffirmed as capacity expansion and biosimilar funnel accelerate, positioning for material CSA revenue ramp from H2 FY27.
financial scorecard: revenue: -26% YoY (INR2,903cr); EBITDA/margin: -70% YoY (INR173cr, ~6% margin); PAT (rptd): -INR472cr loss; PAT (normalized): -INR472cr loss (exceptional Wages Code provision excluded); order book: expanding across Canada, India, emerging markets; net debt: increasing due to INR700cr+ capex, but guidance of <1.5x EBITDA by FY28 maintained
guidance: revenue growth: no FY26/FY27 guidance; margin: to improve with CSA ramp in H2 FY27; order inflow: strong, customer forecasts revised upward; capex/commissioning: INR700cr+ total capex, 75% committed, new capacity to come online H2 FY27
order book & pipeline: Expanding across Canada (pending approvals), India (market opening March), and 80-100 emerging markets (COPP certification expected April); all major customers have increased forecasts.
segment / subsidiary detail: DDC (Drug Device Combination): primary revenue driver delayed by Canadian approvals; Injectables: steady, Bangalore sterile facility undergoing 4-month shutdown for lyophilization capacity upgrade; Soft Gelatine: first oncology NDA approved, partnered with top 10 US generic; Biologics: RFPs 4x YoY, FDA biosimilar guideline changes reducing development cost to $30-40M and timeline to 4-5 years, onboarded US biosimilar major, active EU discussions.
growth verticals / optionality: Biosimilar CDMO opportunity accelerated by Biosecure Act and FDA guideline changes; potential for US/EU beachhead investments; scale-up of batch sizes to improve efficiency and competitiveness; emerging market expansion post-India COPP issuance.
margins & cost dynamics: Current EBITDA margin ~6% due to fixed cost leverage from deferred CSA revenue; margin expansion expected from H2 FY27 as commercial volumes ramp, batch size increases reduce per-unit cost, and capex efficiency improves.
capex / expansion: INR700cr+ total planned capex; 75% committed ($75M) at flagship DDC site; new capacity to be installed by end-FY27; sterile facility in Bangalore undergoing 4-month shutdown for lyophilization/pre-filled syringe upgrades.
capital allocation: Capex funded via strong banking relationships; net debt to peak below 1.5x EBITDA by FY28; long-term goal is debt-free on base business; potential for additional capex in biologics and US/EU expansion.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in Canada/EMs; customer approval timing uncertainty; batch size scale-up regulatory timelines; competitive pressure in India market; working capital tied to customer-owned inventory; execution risk on massive capex ramp.
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and patient; management emphasizes long-term partnerships over short-term revenue, reiterates FY28 guidance despite near-term headwinds, highlights operational excellence and customer trust as core strengths.
non-obvious takeaways: Customer-owned inventory mitigates inventory risk; take-or-pay renegotiations are strategic to lock in longer-term contracts with key partners; FDA biosimilar guideline changes are a structural tailwind, not cyclical; COPP certification from India is the critical enabler for 80+ emerging markets.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
